title: Integrated network pharmacology and experimental validation reveal EGFR/p53/Bcl-2-mediated anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effects of Zedoary Turmeric Oil.
authors: Zhong, Min; Li, Yingpeng; Wang, Hui; Fan, Ni; Chu, Xinhong; Liu, Liang; Zhao, Chengcheng; Sun, Yujiao; Zhang, Shuai; Fu, Hui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药莪术油抗肝癌的分子机制，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法聚焦于TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Curcumae Rhizoma, a traditional Chinese medicine derived from the dried rhizome of Curcuma species, has long been used to treat liver-related disorders. In the classical medical text Taiping Shenghui Fang, it was recorded for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) characterized by Qi stagnation and blood stasis. Its major chemical constituents include curcumin and Zedoary Turmeric Oil (ZTO). While curcumin has been extensively studied for its pharmacological activities, the therapeutic potential and mechanism of ZTO in HCC remain insufficiently understood. AIM: ZTO is a volatile oil fraction extracted from Curcumae Rhizoma, and preliminary studies have suggested its potential anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effects. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of ZTO against HCC through an integrated approach combining network pharmacology and experimental validation. METHODS: An H22 xenograft tumor model was established to evaluate the in vivo anti-tumor efficacy of ZTO. The antiproliferative effects of ZTO on HCC cells were assessed in vitro using MTT and colony formation assays. The synergistic effects of ZTO and sorafenib were evaluated using MTT and tumor sphere-forming assay. The chemical constituents of ZTO were identified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Potential targets of ZTO and HCC were retrieved from public databases, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using the STRING database. Key hub targets were identified using CytoNCA, CytoHubba, and MCODE, followed by molecular dynamics simulations and molecular docking. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were performed using the DAVID database. Following network pharmacology predictions of ZTO's potential mechanism against HCC, we systematically validated these computational findings through experiments in vitro and in vivo. Finally, the pharmacokinetic study of the four active components (curcumol, beta-elemene, germacrone, and curdione) in ZTO was conducted using GC-MS. RESULTS: ZTO significantly inhibited tumor growth in xenograft model. In vitro, ZTO suppressed the proliferation of HCC cells, and it exhibited a synergistic effect when combined with sorafenib. A total of 174 overlapping targets between ZTO and HCC were identified. Among them, EGFR, p53 and Bcl-2 were recognized as key targets. The major compounds and target proteins had a good binding ability in molecular docking and molecular dynamics. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses suggested that ZTO may regulate apoptosis, cell cycle progression, and migration through the EGFR/p53/Bcl-2 signaling axis. Additionally, pathways associated with stem cell pluripotency were significantly enriched. Subsequent experimental validation confirmed that ZTO promoted apoptosis, induced G1-phase arrest, and inhibited cell migration via the EGFR/p53/Bcl-2 axis. Furthermore, ZTO reduced the size of HCC tumor spheres in a dose-dependent manner and downregulated the expression of stemness-related markers, including CD44, CD133, Oct-4, SOX2, and Nanog, both in vitro and in vivo, potentially through modulation of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. Pharmacokinetic analysis indicated that curcumol and curdione exhibited higher bioavailability compared to beta-elemene and germacrone. CONCLUSION: Through an integrated approach combining network pharmacology and experimental validation, this study demonstrates that ZTO exerts anti-HCC effects by inhibiting cell proliferation and migration, inducing apoptosis, and causing G1-phase cell cycle arrest, primarily through modulation of the EGFR/p53/Bcl-2 signaling axis. In addition, ZTO significantly suppresses cancer stemness in HCC by downregulating key stemness-related markers. Finally, the pharmacokinetic study showed curcumol and curdione have higher bioavailability and faster absorption than beta-elemene and germacrone. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights into the anti-HCC activity of ZTO and offer a theoretical foundation for its future clinical application.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：莪术（Curcumae Rhizoma）是一种源自姜黄属（Curcuma）植物干燥根茎的传统中药，长期以来用于治疗肝脏相关疾病。在经典医学文献《太平圣惠方》中，记载其用于治疗以气滞血瘀为特征的肝细胞癌（HCC）。其主要化学成分包括姜黄素和莪术油（ZTO）。尽管姜黄素的药理活性已被广泛研究，但莪术油在肝细胞癌中的治疗潜力及其作用机制仍了解不足。目的：莪术油是从莪术中提取的挥发性油组分，初步研究表明其具有潜在的抗肝细胞癌作用。然而，其潜在机制尚不明确。本研究旨在通过网络药理学与实验验证相结合的综合方法，阐明莪术油抗肝细胞癌的分子机制。方法：建立H22异种移植瘤模型，评估莪术油体内抗肿瘤疗效。采用MTT和集落形成实验评估莪术油对肝细胞癌细胞的体外抗增殖作用。采用MTT和肿瘤球形成实验评估莪术油与索拉非尼的协同效应。通过气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS）鉴定莪术油的化学成分。从公共数据库获取莪术油和肝细胞癌的潜在靶点，并利用STRING数据库构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络。使用CytoNCA、CytoHubba和MCODE识别关键枢纽靶点，随后进行分子动力学模拟和分子对接。利用DAVID数据库进行基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析。在通过网络药理学预测莪术油抗肝细胞癌的潜在机制后，我们通过体外和体内实验系统验证了这些计算发现。最后，采用GC-MS对莪术油中四种活性成分（莪术醇、β-榄香烯、吉马酮和莪术二酮）进行药代动力学研究。结果：莪术油显著抑制异种移植模型中的肿瘤生长。体外实验中，莪术油抑制肝细胞癌细胞的增殖，并与索拉非尼联合使用时表现出协同效应。共鉴定出莪术油与肝细胞癌之间的174个重叠靶点。其中，EGFR、p53和Bcl-2被识别为关键靶点。主要化合物与靶蛋白在分子对接和分子动力学中表现出良好的结合能力。GO和KEGG富集分析提示，莪术油可能通过EGFR/p53/Bcl-2信号轴调控细胞凋亡、细胞周期进程和迁移。此外，与干细胞多能性相关的通路显著富集。后续实验验证证实，莪术油通过EGFR/p53/Bcl-2轴促进细胞凋亡、诱导G1期阻滞并抑制细胞迁移。此外，莪术油以剂量依赖性方式减小肝细胞癌肿瘤球的尺寸，并在体外和体内下调干性相关标志物的表达，包括CD44、CD133、Oct-4、SOX2和Nanog，可能通过调节Wnt/β-catenin信号通路实现。药代动力学分析表明，莪术醇和莪术二酮相比β-榄香烯和吉马酮具有更高的生物利用度。结论：通过网络药理学与实验验证相结合的综合方法，本研究证明莪术油主要通过调节EGFR/p53/Bcl-2信号轴，抑制细胞增殖和迁移、诱导细胞凋亡及引起G1期细胞周期阻滞，从而发挥抗肝细胞癌作用。此外，莪术油通过下调关键干性相关标志物显著抑制肝细胞癌的癌症干性。最后，药代动力学研究表明，莪术醇和莪术二酮相比β-榄香烯和吉马酮具有更高的生物利用度和更快的吸收速度。这些发现为莪术油的抗肝细胞癌活性提供了新的机制见解，并为其未来临床应用奠定了理论基础。
